thought: The user wants me to extract logical reasoning from Daoist/BaZi texts and return a structured JSON with specific fields for each of 10 texts. Let me research these texts to provide accurate logical ex...

entries.logic_thesis: Daily inner cultivation is the practical path: still the mind, gather qi, and return to the One through constant, simple inner work rather than outer ritual.
entries.logic_chain: 1) The Dao is present in ordinary daily life, not only in extraordinary rites. 2) The mind’s restlessness scatters jing, qi, and shen. 3) Stillness and non-action (wuwei) reverse that scattering and gather the three treasures. 4) Continuous ‘inner daily use’ (nei ri yong) builds a stable inner chamber where original nature reappears. 5) When the heart is quiet and breath regulated, the practitioner unites with Lao Jun’s teaching without needing elaborate form. 6) Thus salvation is incremental self-governance, not sudden external grace alone.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Map Day Master strength vs. overacting officials/wealth as ‘scattered mind/qi’ needing stillness. 2) Prefer charts with strong Resource (印) and balanced Companion as capacity for daily quiet cultivation. 3) Time inner work to hours when Day Master is supported (印/比劫 peaks). 4) Treat Fire excess as mental agitation; use Water/Metal seasons for cooling and gathering. 5) Use annual luck that strengthens Resource or softens Officer pressure as windows for meditation progress.
entries.logic_compare: Closer to practical neidan manuals than to liturgical codes: it compresses alchemical aims into daily mind-breath discipline. Unlike 黄庭外景经’s visceral mapping or 入药镜’s dense metaphors, it stresses plain continuity. Versus 无上秘要, it is personal practice, not encyclopedic cosmology.

entries.logic_thesis: Ultimate Daoist knowledge is systematic: hierarchy of heavens, ranks, rites, and cosmology must be ordered so practice and salvation rest on correct structure, not isolated techniques.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Reality is multi-layered (heavens, earths, spirits, ranks). 2) Without a total taxonomy, partial practices misalign with the cosmic order. 3) Collecting and ranking scriptures and methods preserves orthodoxy. 4) Correct rank and rite channel proper spiritual authority. 5) The adept’s path is therefore orientation within a known hierarchy before specialized work. 6) ‘Wushang’ (unsurpassed) means completeness of order, not a single secret formula.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Read the full natal structure as a hierarchy: Day Master center, then stems/branches as ranked ‘offices.’ 2) Identify which ‘ranks’ (官杀印食) dominate and whether they are in correct generative sequence. 3) Prefer luck cycles that restore missing generative links (e.g., Resource→Official when career/authority is blocked). 4) Use elemental hierarchy (生克制化) as the chart’s ‘cosmic protocol’ before applying single-star rules. 5) Treat clashing branches as disorder in the hierarchy needing mediation (合/通关).
entries.logic_compare: Unlike single-theme neidan texts (内日用, 入药镜), 无上秘要 is an encyclopedic architecture of Daoism. It parallels 道藏目录详注 in cataloguing but is substantive content, not mere bibliographic index. Compared with 道门科范大全集, it frames doctrine and cosmology more than liturgical step-lists.

entries.logic_thesis: The body is a sacred landscape: by visualizing and regulating the outer (and implied inner) courts of the Yellow Court, the adept harmonizes viscera, spirits, and longevity.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Each bodily region houses spirits and functions (courts). 2) Disorder of mind or breath disturbs these courts and shortens life. 3) Recitation, visualization, and breath bind consciousness to the correct court. 4) Harmonized courts refine jing to qi and stabilize shen. 5) Longevity and clarity follow from internal governance, not only external medicine. 6) The ‘outer scene’ text still points practice back into the living body as microcosm.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Map Five Viscera to Five Elements and check natal imbalances as ‘court disorders.’ 2) Day Master + Resource = shen stability; weak Resource suggests visualization/breath priority. 3) Earth as center (脾/中宫) — strengthen if chart lacks 戊己/辰戌丑未 balance. 4) Use seasonal branches (四季) for organ-tonifying timing in health luck. 5) Fire-Water axis (心肾) as core: balance 丙丁 vs 壬癸 before chasing wealth stars.
entries.logic_compare: More somatic-cosmographic than 太上老君内日用妙经’s plain daily stillness. Less laboratory alchemy than 太清金液神丹经; less symbolic ‘medicine’ language than 入药镜. Shares microcosm logic with later neidan but in classic Yellow Court form.

entries.logic_thesis: True transformation requires correct materials, fire phases, and timing: the golden liquid divine elixir is produced by lawful process, whether laboratory or body-as-furnace.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Crude matter is not yet elixir; it must be selected and purified. 2) Fire phasing (文武火) and timing govern success or explosion/failure. 3) Correct sequence (collect → refine → nourish → complete) cannot be skipped. 4) Divine efficacy appears only when process matches principle. 5) Error in dose, vessel, or calendar voids the work. 6) Thus alchemy is causal craft under cosmic law, not wishful ritual alone.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Treat Day Master as ‘raw medicine’; Useful God (用神) as the refining agent. 2) Luck periods as fire phases: strong support = 文火 nourishing; harsh Officer/War = 武火 testing. 3) Sequence chart events: establish foundation (印/比) before wealth extraction (财) and authority (官). 4) Avoid ‘incomplete cycles’—acting on partial combinations without waiting for 合化 completion years. 5) Poison/杀 without control = failed furnace; need 食伤 or 印 to regulate.
entries.logic_compare: Shares process discipline with 入药镜 but in classical waidan register of vessels and golden liquid. More technical-causal than 黄庭’s visualization courts. Contrasts with 道门科范’s public liturgy: here the ‘rite’ is the timed fire of the elixir itself.

entries.logic_thesis: Internal alchemy is mirrored in concise maxims: know the true lead and mercury, match yin-yang and firing, and the ‘medicine’ enters so the golden elixir forms in the body.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Scattered metaphors confuse; the mirror-text condenses the essential pairs (lead/mercury, kan/li, movement/stillness). 2) Medicine is already within; it must be recognized, not invented. 3) Wrong timing or forced fire leaks the medicine. 4) Correct coupling of yin-yang reverses aging’s flow. 5) Once medicine ‘enters,’ continuous gentle refinement completes the embryo of immortality. 6) Short verses act as a diagnostic mirror for the practitioner’s state.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Identify true Useful God as ‘true lead’ (what actually rescues the chart). 2) Identify false prosperity (假神/忌神 as false mercury) that looks strong but harms Day Master. 3) Use 调候 (climate adjustment) as firing schedule for extreme cold/hot charts. 4) Combine stems (天干合) as yin-yang pairing years for major refining luck. 5) Track 通关 bridges when two useful elements fail to connect—medicine cannot ‘enter’ without a path.
entries.logic_compare: More compressed and mnemonic than 太清金液神丹经’s extended procedures; more explicitly neidan than early waidan tone. Aligns with 张三丰全集’s later internal-alchemy teaching but in classic Cui/Zhang line brevity. Versus 内日用, it is more technical-symbolic than plain daily advice.

entries.logic_thesis: Communal and priestly efficacy depends on correct liturgical norms: ranks, sequences, offerings, and texts must follow ke-fan (codes) so heaven responds and order is restored.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Daoist action in the world is not only private meditation. 2) Public rites mediate between people, spirits, and heavens. 3) Without standardized codes, rites lose authority and invite disorder. 4) Correct sequence, vestments, documents, and offerings align human petition with celestial bureaucracy. 5) When form is right, response (感应) can occur. 6) Thus salvation of community requires institutional form as much as inner sincerity.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Read Official/Killers (官杀) as ritual authority and rules; their health shows capacity for structured practice/office. 2) Strong Officer with Resource support = lawful ‘code-keeping’ career luck. 3) Chaos in chart (many clashes, no 用神) parallels broken ke-fan—restore sequence before ambition. 4) Use 合/会 as ‘assembled congregation’ years for public or team rites/projects. 5) Prefer luck that stabilizes Officer without crushing Day Master when seeking institutional roles.
entries.logic_compare: Opposite pole from solitary neidan texts (内日用, 入药镜): emphasis is corporate liturgy. More performative-procedural than 无上秘要’s doctrinal encyclopedia, though complementary. Unlike 太上助国救民总真秘要, it is broader ke-yi form rather than specifically crisis-exorcistic statecraft.

entries.name_han: 太上助国救民总真秘要
entries.logic_thesis: True secret methods exist to aid the state and relieve the people: correctly authorized rites, registers, and techniques suppress disaster, disease, and demonic disorder for the public good.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Political and social calamities have spiritual as well as material causes. 2) The Daoist adept with proper registers can intervene. 3) Methods are ‘zong zhen’ (assembled true essentials)—selected for efficacy, not display. 4) Helping nation and people legitimizes the use of powerful techniques. 5) Wrong or unauthorized use harms; correct lineage and intent protect. 6) Thus esoteric skill is framed as civic-therapeutic duty under Heaven.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Charts with strong Officer + output (食伤) = capacity to translate skill into public remedy. 2) Disaster years (刑冲破害, 七杀 uncontrolled) as periods needing ‘救民’ strategy: control, not denial. 3) Use 印星 as mandate/authorization—without it, aggressive 杀 is rogue force. 4) Wealth serving Officer (财生官) as resources directed to institutional relief, not private hoarding. 5) Prefer 七杀有制 patterns when timing crisis-response careers (medicine, security, reform).
entries.logic_compare: Shares ritual power with 道门科范 but aims explicitly at state-people crisis relief and thunder/exorcistic-type essentials. More applied and ‘public goods’ than 黄庭’s body-courts or 金液’s elixir lab. Distinct from bibliographic 道藏目录详注 by being operational secret essentials, not catalogue.

entries.logic_thesis: The Daoist canon must be ordered, titled, and annotated so seekers know what each text is, where it sits, and how to approach the ocean of scriptures without drowning.
entries.logic_chain: 1) The Daozang is vast; unguided reading scatters effort. 2) Cataloguing assigns each work a place (dong, bu, category). 3) Annotations clarify authorship, content, and use. 4) Correct entry enables correct study sequence. 5) Bibliographic clarity is itself a form of transmission. 6) Therefore path-finding meta-knowledge is prerequisite to deep practice of any single classic.
entries.logic_practice: 1) First inventory the whole chart (full pillar scan) before specializing on one star—catalogue before practice. 2) Rank elements by strength like ranking texts by section; know ‘which volume’ your life is in. 3) Use Useful God selection as choosing the right ‘entry text’ among many possible techniques. 4) In luck cycles, identify which ‘department’ (wealth/officer/output) is opening and study/act accordingly. 5) Avoid applying obscure rules before master structure is annotated—parallel to reading notes before esoterica.
entries.logic_compare: Not a cultivation manual but a map of manuals; contrasts with all practice-centered works on this list. Complements 无上秘要’s encyclopedic impulse with Ming bibliographic detail. Versus 张三丰全集 or 灵剑子, it teaches orientation, not method of body or sword-immortality.

entries.logic_thesis: Integrated late Daoist cultivation unites Xing and Ming, martial and still practice, and plain moral clarity so the adept completes both human nature and life-destiny.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Fragmented arts (only sitting, only martial, only theory) leave the work half-done. 2) Xing (nature) and Ming (life/fate-energy) must be cultivated together. 3) Ethical conduct stabilizes the vessel for higher work. 4) Internal alchemy language is reconciled with accessible instruction. 5) Embodiment (including boxing/health arts in the tradition) and stillness correct each other. 6) Completion is full-person transformation, not collection of isolated feats.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Balance Day Master (Ming/vessel) with Resource and Output (Xing/expression)—neither dead quiet nor pure leakage. 2) Read 食伤 as creative/martial expression; 印 as stillness/study—both needed in sequence. 3) Officer as moral-ritual constraint: useful when soft, crushing when wild. 4) Luck that alternates support for body (比劫/印) and spirit-use (食伤/官杀制化) suits xing-ming dual cultivation. 5) Avoid extremes: pure wealth chasing without Resource = Ming drained; pure yin still without engagement = Xing inert.
entries.logic_compare: Synthesizes threads found separately in 内日用 (daily practice), 入药镜 (elixir theory), and embodied arts beyond 黄庭’s classical recitation. Less institutional than 科范/助国救民; more person-centered complete path. Broader and later in tone than early 太清 waidan scripture.

entries.logic_thesis: The ‘numinous sword’ is the adept’s disciplined spiritual force: with correct method, intent, and purity, one cuts ignorance and demonic obstruction and advances toward immortal realization.
entries.logic_chain: 1) Obstacles to the Dao include inner afflictions and outer malign influences. 2) Ordinary effort lacks a sharp, concentrated instrument. 3) The ling jian symbolizes refined qi-intent that can sever delusion. 4) Training the sword (method + virtue) protects the practice and clears the path. 5) Mastery turns weapon into wisdom—destruction of illusion, not aggression for its own sake. 6) Thus martial-spiritual imagery encodes decisive, focused cultivation.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Treat 七杀 or strong Metal as ‘sword qi’—valuable only when controlled (食伤泄 or 印化). 2) Uncontrolled Kill = violent chaos; controlled Kill = decisive breakthrough luck. 3) Time major ‘cuts’ (career change, ending toxins) to years when 杀 is合 or 制. 4) Day Master weak + sharp Officer/Kill needs Resource tempering before using sword strategies. 5) Output (食伤) as sword-handling skill: technique without virtue (印/官 balance) fails the ling (numinous) criterion.
entries.logic_compare: More martial-exorcistic in metaphor than 黄庭’s organ courts or 内日用’s quiet dailyism. Shares ‘clearing obstruction’ purpose with 助国救民 but at personal-immortal scale. Distinct from 入药镜’s lead-mercury mirror: here the key image is the numinous blade of intent rather than medicinal pairing.
